newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Top U.S. coffee assoc'n sees high arabica prices.
newsitem.headline: Top U.S. coffee assoc'n sees high arabica prices.

text.p: A top U.S. coffee association said on Thursday it expected prices for high quality arabica coffee to remain at high levels.

"It's obvious to everyone in the trade that consumers want better qualities but the availability of high-quality coffees is going to decrease which will push up prices," Ted Lingle, executive director of the Specialty Coffee Association of America told Reuters during a tea and coffee symposium in Vienna.
He added that recent wild fluctuations in the world coffee market "signalled that we are going towards a much higher average price level" for high quality mild arabicas.
"The average price is going to be higher. I would not be surprised to see the mild arabica price between October 1997 and November 1998 at an average of $2 per pound," Lingle added.
